parole.testo: From German Bremse, from Middle Low German premese, derived from Middle Low German premen (“to squeeze, press together”).
for- + veksle, from German verwechseln and Middle Low German vorwesselen.

parole.significato: to anger, to irritate, incite, enrage
parole.testo: From German hitzen (“to heat”) and Middle Low German hessen (“to drive forward”).
From German nüchtern (“sober, matter-of-fact”), from Middle Low German nuchterne, an early loan from Latin nocturnus (“nocturnal”).

parole.significato: to arouse, to excite, to incite, to stir up (a person to feel strong emotion or act emotionally)
parole.testo: From op (“up”) + hidse (“to arouse, to incense”), the latter a combination of borrowings from German hitzen (“to heat”) and Middle Low German hissen (“to drive forward, act upon”). Compare Swedish upphetsa, German aufhetzen, Dutch ophitsen.

parole.significato: a shaft (vertical passage, e.g. a well, elevator, chute)
parole.testo: Via German Schacht, from Middle Low German schacht, from Old Saxon skaft, from Proto-Germanic *skaftaz. Doublet of skaft.
From German ändern, derived from the adjective anderer (“other”) (Danish anden). Compare also the synonym forandre, from Middle Low German veranderen.
